# Ordinary-server transport evidence

This is a documentation supplement to N01, not a captured server response or a new enumerated JSON fixture. The N01 manifest and its fixture inventory are unchanged. No live request was used to write it.

## Versioned public sources

The parent session fetched these public documents while planning N04. The implementation session used the quoted evidence and the existing offline schema excerpts, without network access.

- [Herdr v0.9.0 socket API](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herdrdev/herdr/v0.9.0/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/socket-api.mdx), "Socket transport". "Herdr uses newline-delimited JSON over a local socket. On Unix, that socket is a Unix domain socket. On Windows, it is a named pipe." "Send one request per line" with `{"id":"req_1","method":"ping","params":{}}`. "A successful response includes the same id" with `{"id":"req_1","result":{"type":"pong"}}`. "Event subscriptions keep the connection open after the initial response."
- The same document, "Socket paths". Default `~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock`, named session `~/.config/herdr/sessions/<name>/herdr.sock`. Resolution order is explicit CLI `--session`, `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `HERDR_SESSION`, default. `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH` is the low-level override. N04 does not reconstruct default paths or XDG policy. Its raw adapter requires an explicit inherited socket path. Existing CLI reads keep the CLI's own resolution, with the entire environment frozen.
- [Herdr v0.9.0 plugins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herdrdev/herdr/v0.9.0/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/plugins.mdx), "Commands and environment". Runtime commands run in the plugin directory. Herdr injects `HERDR_SOCKET_PATH`, `HERDR_BIN_PATH`, `HERDR_ENV=1`, plugin ID/root/config/state/context, and available workspace/tab/pane IDs. An actual pane ID differs from the focused-context hint. The document recommends `HERDR_BIN_PATH` for portable CLI use, including Windows. It does not define a portable raw CLI command accepting protocol JSON on stdin.
- [Herdr v0.9.0 connecting machines](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/herdrdev/herdr/v0.9.0/docs/next/website/src/content/docs/connecting-machines.mdx), read by the parent before implementation. Custom commands and plugins execute on the selected server. A pane's inherited CLI socket continues to address that server when the client changes its selected machine. This is execution-location evidence, not a client-control authorization contract.

The existing `schema-excerpts.json` records installed offline Herdr 0.9.0 metadata, protocol 22. It supplies `session.snapshot`, workspace/tab/pane list and focus request shapes, `agent.list`, response discriminators, required fields, and `ErrorBody { code, message }`. Exact focus uses `workspace_id`, `tab_id`, or `pane_id`. The directional pane CLI is not an exact-pane substitute.

## Implemented contract

`OrdinaryServer` has typed workspace, tab, pane, and agent reads and `focus` taking a qualified `LiveTarget`. Raw method strings stay inside the adapter. Inventory still uses the documented existing CLI lists; N05 owns inventory conversion. Each CLI process has frozen executable resolution, arguments, environment including absent route variables, and cwd. Missing cwd fails child startup instead of substituting `/`. Notifications do not enter JSON parsing.

Raw focus connects to the explicit socket on Linux and macOS. It sends one compact JSON request plus newline, generates a unique invocation-local request ID, and checks the returned ID. It does not send JSON to CLI stdin. Before each mutation it reads `session.snapshot` and enables exact target kinds only for version `0.9.0` and protocol `22`. Other versions remain unknown rather than inheriting compatibility from the plugin manifest. A version string grants no identity or authorization. Explicit unsupported-method rejections disable only that kind. The schema leaves error codes open; N04 conservatively recognizes `unknown_method`, `unsupported_method`, and `method_not_found`. Other structured errors reject only that request, without guessing their meaning or rotating scope.

CLI IDs belong to the CLI. The parser requires a nonempty string ID, but does not impose the historical `cli:*` spelling or compare it with Navigator's raw IDs. Both paths reject malformed envelopes, duplicate keys, conflicting success/error fields, wrong discriminators, missing or mistyped required fields, and trailing JSON in the received payload. Raw NDJSON requires the terminating newline. The client consumes one response frame and closes its connection; it does not subscribe or wait for a second frame. Bytes a peer sends after that completed exchange cannot qualify another request.

Default limits are two seconds per request, 64 KiB request bytes, 8 MiB inventory stdout, 64 KiB focus stdout, and 64 KiB stderr. Focus negotiation and mutation share one absolute deadline. Limits are injectable for tests. Nonblocking socket connect/write/read and process pipe polling check the deadline. Parsing has a byte cap and checks the deadline before accepting its result. OS spawn and cleanup calls, and an individual parser call, cannot promise real-time preemption.

The process runner drains stdout and stderr together, writes optional bounded stdin, and polls without reader threads. On exit, timeout, overflow, or I/O failure it kills the child's process group and reaps the direct child. It does not reap the leader before group cleanup. Inherited output pipes remain deadline-bound even when the leader has exited. A descendant that deliberately leaves the process group cannot be killed through that group. Navigator still closes its pipes and returns within its polling deadline; it cannot reap unrelated descendants or provide a sandbox. Custom notification sound playback and optional non-Herdr providers remain outside this runner.

Errors distinguish `NotSent`, structured `Rejected`, and `Unknown` mutation outcomes. A focus negotiation failure is `NotSent` for the mutation. Once any mutation bytes have been written, transport or acknowledgement failure is `Unknown`. No mutation retries or fallback commands run. Errors do not print route paths, environment, stderr, or arbitrary server messages. A successful focus response acknowledges the ordinary server, not a transition in the invoking client.

## Scope and filesystem assumptions

A normal, unchanged Herdr-managed plugin invocation provides process/server co-location under the documented runtime contract. N04 requires an explicit inherited socket, `HERDR_ENV=1`, nonempty plugin ID and root, and known cwd before accepting that relation. It freezes the invocation before requests. This is a trust assumption about Herdr's launcher and the caller's unchanged environment. It is not authentication against an external caller who overrides those variables before launch. No socket path comparison, local path existence check, version string, context workspace ID, or correlation ID authenticates a client.

Only process-owned paths gain ordinary reuse/create permission under that assumption. A `Reported` path still cannot cross the local filesystem interface, even for a co-located invocation. Unknown invocations and raw injected routes without that runtime contract do not gain filesystem permission. Quick Actions retains its existing ordinary plugin-action dispatch without requiring filesystem co-location.

Transport uncertainty or a change in previously observed version/protocol rotates the ephemeral scope, clears picker/current-target hints, removes co-location and capability observations, and marks freshness stale. App applies failures before converting collected inventory, so a successful response from the old generation cannot acquire new-generation identities. A healthy refresh preserves scope. Later healthy reads do not restore cleared co-location from startup environment; a new invocation is required. Structured target or unsupported-operation rejection does not rotate scope.

Protocol 22 has no durable server incarnation or client identity in the snapshot. A silent restart that reuses IDs and the same socket/version cannot be detected. Checking version before focus reduces compatibility mistakes, not this identity limitation. Persistent live-target replay and client-wide history remain disabled pending later work. Linux tests use only synthetic sockets and temporary CLI stubs. macOS compilation/runtime and other-platform behavior still need platform CI. Other platforms return explicit unsupported transport errors.

N04 is not all-pane conversion, combined navigation, client-authorized focus, or native new-workspace support. Agent rows still use the legacy terminal dispatch until N05/N06. Creation and template behavior is restored only under the managed-plugin assumption; N06 must finish action revalidation and release qualification. N07 still owns persisted marks and jump-back, and S01 still owns the failed-overlay lifecycle release gate.
